newsitem.title: FRANCE: L'Oreal seeks half of sales outside Europe.
newsitem.headline: L'Oreal seeks half of sales outside Europe.

text.p: Cosmetics giant L'Oreal wants to generate half its sales outside western Europe by the year 2000, compared with 40 percent today and 13 percent in 1991, chairman Lindsay Owen-Jones said in an interview.
He also said the group aimed to increase sales to 100 billion francs by 2001 from 60.35 billion in 1996.
"Our objective for the end of the century is to generate half our sales outside Europe," Owen-Jones told the newspaper Le Figaro. He said the group favoured internal growth.
He also said L'Oreal was moving toward concentrating its products under several major, globally recognized brands.

"Hundreds of brands that are too small or too local will disappear. We've seen that in the past. In France, for instance, the brand Ricils has been progressively overtaken by Gemey and the latter may in the medium term become part of Maybelline," the U.S. cosmetics brand recently acquired by L'Oreal, he said.
